summary: Configured a persistent NFSv4.2 share from node1 `/srv/nfs/shared` to node2 `/mnt/shared`. Both systems use `dataops` UID/GID 4500, the shared directory is mode 2770, and ownership/data survived sequential restarts of both nodes.
actions_performed: Installed NFS utilities on both nodes.
Created the `dataops` user and group with UID/GID 4500 on both nodes.
Configured node1’s writable SELinux-aware NFS export and firewall access.
Mounted the export on node2 and persisted it in `/etc/fstab`.
Verified bidirectional file creation, ownership, and permissions.
Restarted node1 and node2 individually and verified changed boot IDs and complete recovery.

evidence.summary: Both nodes show dataops UID/GID 4500; the server directory and client mountpoint use dataops:dataops and mode 2770.
Shows the active/enabled NFS service, writable export restricted to node2, SELinux configuration, listener, persistent export configuration, and final healthy state.
Shows the `/etc/fstab` NFSv4.2 entry and the recovered live mount after reboot.

evidence.requirement: Consistent cross-node access, ownership, and permissions
evidence.summary: Files created from either node are readable on the other and retain dataops:dataops ownership with mode 660; a new post-restart file was also verified across nodes.
Healthy baseline boot ID 03408ac4-bfe4-4151-98bd-1966b0a205af, restart acknowledgement, changed boot ID baf7037d-8eb7-405d-8387-95a82e8e73d9, and recovered service/export/mount/data.

Healthy baseline boot ID 646e5f74-dc0e-45e7-9746-226c4351af28, restart acknowledgement, changed boot ID 4280a288-3598-4504-a9c1-5ea989160f68, and recovered mount, identity, permissions, and shared data.
